title: Fine-Tuning a 3B Clinical LLM
description: Fine-tuned a 3B clinical LLM to extract survival predictors from post-cystectomy records with 96% accuracy on the study's defined extraction task.
detailSummary: This research tests whether a compact model can match a frontier-model baseline on a narrowly defined clinical extraction task and preserve the value of manually abstracted data for downstream survival prediction.
detailBullets: Matched GPT-5.2 at 96% accuracy on the study's specific clinical information-extraction task using a 3B-parameter model.
Used LoRA fine-tuning to structure predictors from post-cystectomy bladder-cancer records.
Evaluated whether model-extracted predictors could retain the five-year survival-prediction performance obtained from manually extracted information.

title: Streamlining Paper Selection
description: Expanded an LLM-assisted literature-screening workflow to 3,200+ records, cutting the number requiring manual review by more than half.
detailSummary: This workflow uses LLMs for first-pass paper triage, reducing manual screening burden while keeping inclusion and exclusion decisions available for human review. An expanded evaluation is currently under review.
detailBullets: Expanded the original 121-record conference study to more than 3,200 literature records.
Reduced the set requiring manual review by more than half through model-guided inclusion and exclusion decisions.
Kept structured decision logs so reviewers could inspect results and resolve borderline papers rather than treating the model as the final reviewer.

title: Subtype-First Breast Cancer Classification
description: Led a 10+ student team comparing direct benign/malignant training with a subtype-first approach that maps predicted tumor subtypes to the final binary label.
detailSummary: Instead of training only on benign and malignant labels, the models first learned the eight tumor subtypes. Each predicted subtype was then mapped deterministically to its benign or malignant class; subtype accuracy itself was not the final endpoint.
detailBullets: Compared direct binary training with subtype-first training on the BreakHis histopathology dataset.
On the internal test split, subtype-first training improved binary accuracy by 23.7 percentage points for Bag of Visual Words and 11.2 points for the CNN.
The subtype-first ViT reported 98.9% binary accuracy and 0.989 AUC on the study split; external validation is still needed to assess generalizability.

title: Image-to-Item Identification
description: Built an AI-assisted intake pipeline that identifies donated medical supplies from photos and converts shipping-box images into structured inventory records.
detailSummary: Blueprints for Pangaea redistributes surplus medical supplies to communities with limited access. This system reduces repetitive cataloging by turning photos of incoming donations into standardized item records for chapter teams.
detailBullets: Implemented automated product naming from photos using Python, the OpenAI Agent SDK, and API integrations.
Turned donation-box snapshots into structured inventory records for review instead of requiring every field to be entered from scratch.
Integrated the workflow with internal inventory tooling that has tracked more than 37,700 items in 2026 through July.

title: Automated Item Pricing
description: Developed a valuation pipeline that compares identified medical supplies across market sources to produce consistent, reviewable fair-market estimates.
detailSummary: Consistent valuation helps the nonprofit report the scale of redistributed supplies to partners and donors. This pipeline standardizes market comparisons while leaving final values reviewable by the operations team.
detailBullets: Automated pricing normalization by looking up identified items across market sources using Apps Script and Python.
Supports valuation and reporting for more than $1M in supplies redistributed annually.
Blueprints for Pangaea has redistributed approximately $10M in medical supplies over its lifetime.

title: Inventory Management Case Study
description: Completed a one-time inventory analytics case study that identified operational bottlenecks and informed medical-supply redistribution planning.
detailSummary: This one-time case study examined more than 12,000 inventory records to understand donation patterns, surface operational inefficiencies, and inform redistribution decisions.
detailBullets: Built interactive views for donation volume, inventory composition, and supply movement.
Analyzed more than 12,000 item records to identify patterns and operational bottlenecks.
Presented findings and technology recommendations to support redistribution planning across partner sites.

title: Population Health Leaders
description: Engineered an automated web scraping pipeline to identify and catalog population health decision-makers across U.S. hospital systems, building a structured database for targeted outreach.
detailSummary: This project converted fragmented public information about U.S. health-system leadership into a structured dataset for population-health outreach and research.
detailBullets: Built a Python pipeline to discover and extract population-health leadership information from public web sources.
Normalized titles, organizations, and contact context into a consistent dataset.
Identified more than 500 relevant leaders while reducing repetitive manual research.
